findings.claim: The fail-fast 'Multiple crypto providers loaded' IllegalStateException is replaced by order-based selection. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200, so on a tie the stable sort leaves the choice to ServiceLoader/classpath order. A FIPS deployment that picks up a stray non-FIPS jar can now silently run on the non-FIPS provider.
findings.evidence: All three seats cite `return 200` at DefaultCryptoProvider.java:83-84, WildFlyElytronProvider.java:76-77 and FIPS1402Provider.java:114-115. Losers are logged only at debug. Base threw IllegalStateException. Affected init() callers: KeycloakApplication.java:89, admin-cli Globals.java:44 (dist packages both default and fips1402 jars), testsuite CryptoInitRule.java:14, AuthzClient.create. Quarkus is unaffected (setProvider at KeycloakRecorder.java:214). Proposed red test (superpowers): two order-200 providers on the ServiceLoader path; assert init() throws. It throws on base and returns a provider on HEAD. Not run.
findings.reason: Accepted. Three seats agree and the evidence is source-cited. Before fixing, it must be made red with the proposed two-provider ServiceLoader test. Smallest fix: keep the throw when the top two orders are equal.

findings.claim: `int order()` is added as an abstract method on the public CryptoProvider SPI with no default. External implementations stop compiling. Already-compiled ones loaded via ServiceLoader throw AbstractMethodError when detectProvider's comparator calls order(), which crashes CryptoIntegration.init.
findings.evidence: Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order) in detectProvider. keycloak-common is consumed outside this repo, e.g. the keycloak-client authz-client copy of AuthzClientCryptoProvider. All in-repo implementations are updated (Fips1402StrictCryptoProvider inherits). Reasoned, not run. Seat severities ranged from Minor to Important; normalised to Important because the result is a runtime crash of init.
findings.reason: Accepted. Four seats agree. Red test: a provider compiled against the base interface, loaded alongside another provider, must throw AbstractMethodError on HEAD. Smallest fix: make order() a default method.

findings.claim: One default KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") key is used for ES256, ES384 and ES512. The ES384/ES512 tests never use their own curves, so the DER long-form length paths (ASN1Encoder.writeLength / ASN1Decoder.readLength for length > 127) and full-width P-521 integers are never exercised.
findings.evidence: Test lines 42 and 65-71. The default curve gives a DER sequence of about 70 bytes. superpowers' standalone harness passed 500 signatures per curve on P-256/384/521, including the long-form path, so this is a coverage gap, not a codec bug.
findings.reason: Accepted as a test gap. Generate one key per curve (secp256r1/384r1/521r1).

findings.claim: AuthzClient.create now calls JVM-global CryptoIntegration.init, and the first caller wins. If only the stub provider is visible, AuthzClientCryptoProvider is fixed for the JVM. getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JDK keystore provider, so BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER becomes e.g. 'SUN'. Later Keycloak code then gets UnsupportedOperationException, and a later init (e.g. KeycloakApplication) does nothing.
findings.evidence: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:61-66. init is a no-op once cryptoProvider is set. Mitigation: on the testsuite classpath crypto-default (200) beats the stub (100), and the module is testsuite-only. No concrete failure found.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by fewer than three seats.

coverage: Files: all four seats report 12/12 files reviewed. open-code-review's tool skipped META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider (unsupported extension) and ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java (default path); the seat read both by hand. superpowers checked the whitespace-only hunks in DefaultCryptoProvider.java, FIPS1402Provider.java and CryptoProvider.java only for being whitespace. ponytail reviewed only for over-engineering. mattpocock checked the ASN.1 internals only for correctness on the ES256/384/512 paths. Axes not run: the gate was not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored by executed checks, and nothing was built or tested in the repo. The only executed evidence is superpowers' standalone javac harness outside the repo. There is no spec: only the commit title, and issue #33831 was not fetched. The standards axis ran against CONTRIBUTING.md and PR-CHECKLIST.md. No reviewer from another model family took a correctness seat. Left unchecked: whether the Elytron/FIPS test profiles ever put two order-200 providers on one classpath, and whether the Maven BOM manages the hamcrest version. No red tests have been written yet: the two Important main-list findings each have a proposed failing test that has not been run. No finding was rejected, because no seat report disproves another's claim.
